- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; apply downward correction proportional to sentiment swing magnitude.
- Model consistently underestimates 30-day horizon if recent sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); add 0.5–1.5% bias upward for longer horizons.
- If last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply 1–3% downward correction after 10–15 days of trend.
